info.title: VolStrata Public API
info.summary: Options-gamma, greeks, flow, valuation and market-context capabilities, projected from the capability catalogue.
info.description:
Generated from the published capability catalogue.

Every path is the canonical `/api/v1` spelling — the ONE surface (the /api/v2 alias is retired).

Each operation carries its plan/entitlement floor (`x-plan-tier` slug, `x-plan-tier-name` customer-facing name, `x-policy-key`). Widget-feeding JSON reads fold in the shared `freshness` contract (`components.schemas.Freshness`) and the `delivery` contract (`components.schemas.Delivery`), which states whether a body is the live or a delayed lane and what would clear the delay. A small set of published literal-path reads (the daily-proof scorecard, the forecast backtest, the exposure projection and the Master Read) are projected alongside the catalogue.

TELLING OUR REFUSALS FROM THE EDGE'S (write your client against this): every refusal issued by this API is RFC 9457 JSON (`application/problem+json`) carrying a `type` URL, a stable `code`, a `request_id`, and `ok: false`. If a refusal body is NOT JSON, it never reached us — it came from the CDN edge, which answers in `text/plain` (measured example: the Python stdlib's default `Python-urllib/*` User-Agent is refused 403 at the edge with a plain-text `error code: 1010` before we ever see the request; set any User-Agent, or use `requests`/`curl`). And check the HTTP status before the body shape: a rate-limit refusal is `429` with `code: "rate_limited"` and `ok: false` — a collector that only reads `body["series"]` off a 429 records a normal empty day, which is a silent wrong answer, not a missing one.

get.description: `gex.bars` capability. Public (Free tier). Advertised canonical route. Alias of GET /api/v1/research/gex/<ticker>.
`gex.levels` capability. Public (Free tier). Advertised canonical route. Alias of GET /api/v1/research/levels/<ticker>.

Bulk scalar metrics off the latest cached frame: net GEX, regime, zero-gamma, max-pain, walls, EM bounds, ATM IV, skew. `regime` is derived at serve time from the values printed in this same body and `regime_basis` names the definition used — `net_gex_sign` (the sign of `net_gex_bn`) when a net figure is present, else `spot_vs_zero_gamma` (spot vs `zg`). The two definitions agree at the daily close but genuinely disagree on a meaningful share of intraday frames, so compare `regime` across endpoints only together with its basis.

The zero-gamma flip scalar plus the current regime. `regime` is derived from this body's own `spot` vs `gamma_flip` and `regime_basis` says so (`spot_vs_zero_gamma`) — reproducible from the response itself. Note the sibling net-GEX-sign definition (dealergamma.history, gex.metrics when net is present) agrees at the daily close but can disagree intraday.

get.description: `fundamentals.company` capability. Public (Free tier). Advertised canonical route. Alias of GET /api/v1/fundamentals/<ticker>.

One row per session: net dealer gamma, zero-gamma, spot, walls, regime + `regime_basis` (which definition labelled the row), opex/quad-witch flags. `days=` is a trailing calendar window clamped 5..400; the body echoes `days_requested`, the resolved `window_start`, and `corpus_exhausted: true` when the stored history already starts inside the window — i.e. a wider `days=` cannot add rows, the corpus is simply everything that exists.
`dealergamma.tickers` capability. Public (Free tier). Advertised canonical route. Alias of GET /api/v1/dealer-gamma/tickers.

The 0DTE gamma-pin magnet: a live `current` block, the per-tick intraday `series`, and a session `summary`. On a DATED call (`date=YYYY-MM-DD`) the `series`/`summary` are that session's and `current` is null unless the requested date IS the live session — `current` is a live block and is never stamped onto a historical day. A malformed `date` is refused with a 400 rather than silently serving the latest session. Rows carry `regime` with a `regime_basis` naming its SOURCE (`snapshot` | `levels_row`): a sourced label is the producer's own and is NOT re-derivable from the row's printed numbers — for a reproducible intraday regime read, collect `positive` (spot vs the printed zero_gamma) instead. The two readings agree at the session close; the divergence is intraday.

`orderflow.series` capability. Requires the Ultra plan or above. The per-second Order Flow series behind the Order Flow page. WHAT IT IS: a classified session accumulation — prints are attributed to a trade side by VolStrata's proprietary trade-side model over option-chain data, then netted per second into greek-flow totals. WHAT IT IS NOT: an exchange order book, market-by-order depth, a raw per-print tape, or venue-attributed flow — none of those are emitted, and none can be reconstructed from this body. Accumulators reset at the 09:30 ET session open. Returns parallel arrays under `series` (one per requested field, all aligned to `series.t` epoch seconds) plus `cursor` for an incremental `since=` poll, `n_points`, `units`, `completeness`, `available` and `warming`. A field the substrate cannot compute is absent or null — never a synthesised zero. This route REFUSES below the floor (401 anon / 403 under-tier); it does not serve a delayed body — for the freemium delayed variant use `orderflow.impulse`.

get.description: `state.regime` capability. Requires the Pro plan or above. The 0-100 regime scalar plus the structural panel (per-strike lens levels, walls, flip) computed over the recent stored frames for one greek. Positioning structure, not a price forecast and not a trade signal. `window` is how many stored frames the scalar scans; a frame history too thin to score returns the scalar as null with the reason on the body rather than a fabricated midpoint. Access has two independent axes: this capability path REFUSES below the Pro floor (401 anon / 402 under-tier), while the .json alias also serves a free SPX-only body under the standard anonymous 15-minute plan delay — that delayed body's `delivery.upgrade_tier` names the cheapest plan that lifts the DELAY, which is below this capability's floor; the two figures answer different questions and both are correct. This is a LIVE rolling read with no dated history: `date=`/`day=` are refused (400), point-in-time reads are `/api/v1/state/<ticker>?at=`, and the collected label history (recorded forward from 2026-09-01) is `/api/v1/state/regime/history.json` at this same Pro floor.

get.description: `state.ladder` capability. Requires the Pro plan or above for LIVE data. WHAT IT IS: a classified session accumulator built from option-chain data by VolStrata's proprietary trade-side model, reset at the 09:30 ET session open. get.description: `stats.greeks.wall_migration` capability. 🌊 CHARACTER, purely descriptive — no baseline is claimed. Over 63 independent SPX sessions (2026-09-01 cut) the call wall ends the session on a different strike than it opened on in 79.4% of them (50/63, Wilson 67.8-87.5%), moving a median 50 points at maximum excursion across a median 4 distinct strikes; the put wall, 74.6% (47/63). Event-weighted, one session one vote. Says nothing about direction.

`stats.greeks.charm_close_tightness` capability. 🌊 CHARACTER — NULL, published as one. Does heavy aggregate charm into the close produce a tighter closing range, as the dealer-hedging story predicts? Over 64 independent SPX sessions (2026-09-01 cut, graded to the real 16:15 index-option close), Spearman rho = +0.059 at p = 0.64, with the sign opposite to the hypothesis and a non-monotone quartile table. There is no relationship here.

`stats.greeks.open_iv_skew_range` capability. 🌊 CHARACTER — SPLIT. Opening ATM IV at 10:00 ET vs the remaining session's realized range: rho = +0.517, p = 1.4e-05 over 63 sessions — significant and uninteresting, because implied volatility forecasting realized range is implied volatility doing its job. Opening SKEW, the genuinely open half, is a null: rho = +0.052, p = 0.69 over 60 sessions, on a fixed-moneyness wing proxy (the true 25-delta risk reversal held only 27 sessions at the 2026-08-31 census, below the 30-session floor). 2026-09-01 cut.

`stats.greeks.zg_distance_range` capability. 🌊 CHARACTER — NULL. Does the distance from spot to zero gamma at 10:00 ET predict how BIG the rest of the session's range is? Over 63 independent SPX sessions (2026-09-01 cut), rho = +0.224 at p = 0.077 — short of the pre-registered p < 0.05 — over a NON-MONOTONE quartile table, which is the shape of noise rather than of a finding. An underpowered maybe, not a lead; it re-runs honestly at 150+ sessions.

`stats.greeks.oi_vs_volume_wall` capability. 🎯 DIRECTION-adjacent — CONFOUNDED NULL, and the most instructive row in this set: the pre-registered test PASSED and the result is still not a finding. Across 34 divergent sessions (2026-09-01 cut) the volume wall beat the OI wall at marking the call-side extreme (OI 9/34, Wilson upper bound 0.431, binomial p = 0.0090) — but the volume wall simply sits nearer spot (median 18.4 pts vs 47.6) and the extreme lands a median 22.3 pts from spot, so 'whichever level is nearer spot wins' scores 76.5% (p = 0.0029) and explains the outcome better. NO claim is made that either book's wall is the better level; it is served descriptively with its confound block attached.

`stats.greeks.vanna_flip_expansion` capability. 🌊 CHARACTER — NOT MEASURED, and the reason is the finding. Only 10 vanna sign-flip events exist across 3 independent sessions, against a floor of 30, so this renders ACCRUING with its honest count and NEVER a rate: aggregate vanna is positive on 95.8% of frames (11,096/11,586) and holds one sign all day in 58 of 62 sessions (2026-08-31 census), so a 'vanna sign flip' is not a viable event on this book. Its null is time-of-day matched, pre-committed for exactly that reason.

`stats.greeks.dex_vex_direction` capability. 🎯 DIRECTION — IT FAILS, and it is published BECAUSE that was promised in writing before it ran (the pre-registration was committed ahead of the results). Net delta exposure calls the next hour 52.89% of the time (201/380 hourly marks over 64 independent sessions, 2026-09-01 cut), Wilson 0.4787-0.5786, against this sample's OWN majority up-rate of 50.00% — the lower bound does not clear it, so `beats_baseline` is false. Net vanna (the `vex` field carries VANNA, not vega) scores 47.97% (177/369), below its 50.68% baseline outright. The regime split renders NOT MEASURED rather than borrow an 11%-adrift field. This is a clean 'checked, and no' with a real N — not a signal.

`stats.pin_reconciliation` capability. ⚠️ NOT PRE-REGISTERED — an unplanned finding, published in its own row so it can never borrow the eight studies' receipt, and it outranks the reconciliation it fell out of. Both max-pain pipelines (did-it-hold's F7b and /pin-accuracy) agree EXACTLY — identical outcomes on all 78 gradeable sessions (2026-09-01 cut), one shared grader — and both sit UNDER their own honest null: max pain pins 14.1% (11/78) at the 0.25% band while the trivial 'assume the close lands near yesterday's close' pins 29.5% (23/78) over the same sessions. Both modules' own comments said that control had never been run. The null is window-sensitive and the caveat travels with the number.

`accuracy.did_it_hold` capability. Public (Free tier). The honest daily-proof scorecard: for each recent session, did the published key levels settled at the prior close - the call wall, the put wall and the zero-gamma flip - HOLD, BREAK, or go UNTESTED against that session's own realised high, low and close. A level the day never traded to is reported UNTESTED and excluded from the hit-rate. Read-only; never 500s - a thin history degrades to an honest empty board carrying a `reason`.

get.description: `forecast.backtest` capability. Public (Free tier). The scarcity-immune companion to the live forecast scoreboard: a walk-forward, out-of-sample backtest of the served forecast cone over our own retained session history (windows never span the overnight reset). Reports per-horizon MAE and 95% coverage for the served cone plus a skill ratio against a naive random-walk baseline. This is a backtest, NOT a live track record. Never 500s - an unrun harness degrades to `available:false`.

`exposure.projection` capability. Requires the Pro plan or above. The Exposure Projection Heatmap engine: the CURRENT dealer book re-priced across a hypothetical price x forward-session-time grid for one greek lens, returning the signed-exposure matrix, the auto-extracted peak/trough ridge levels and the realised price path for the overlay. Requires a signed-in first-party session; anonymous gets 401. Positioning-only, not a price forecast.

get.description: `state.at` capability. Requires the Pro plan or above. The POINT-IN-TIME market state: the nearest STORED frame at-or-before `at`, in the SAME shape as `/api/v1/state/regime.json` (transparent 0-100 regime scalar + REAL structural per-strike panel). Omit `at` for the live frame. HONEST by construction: the returned `ts` is the frame's own real epoch (it may be earlier than the requested `at` - nearest-at-or-before, never fabricated) and `at_requested` echoes the parsed cursor. Reuses the existing snapshot store (no parallel history). Intraday history is SPX-only; alt tickers return the latest real frame with a note. History depth is gated by the caller's plan (free/anon: today only). Never 500s - degrades to an honest `available:false`.

A Pro+/first-party read (anonymous or below-tier gets 401); the endpoint returns `{enabled:false}` when the framing surface is not currently published. Freshness.description: Additive data-freshness contract. Widget-feeding JSON reads fold this in under a top-level `freshness` key so a client can render an honest 'as of … / N s ago / stale' state from one uniform shape. `live == not stale` is the positive liveness gate (known timestamp AND age within the feed's threshold); an unknown timestamp is honestly `stale:true` / `live:false`, never faked fresh. Per-feed staleness thresholds (seconds): STALE_BREADTH=2700s, STALE_DAILY=86400s, STALE_EOD=90000s, STALE_FAST_INTRADAY=180s, STALE_NEWS=3600s, STALE_SLOW_ROLLUP=900s.

as_of.description: epoch-ms of the data's own timestamp; null when unknown

age_seconds.description: server_now - as_of, floored at 0; null when unknown

live.description: known timestamp AND age within the feed threshold

source.description: short human SUBJECT label, e.g. 'SPX chain'

Delivery.description: Additive delivery contract, folded in under a top-level `delivery` key alongside `freshness`. Answers WHY data is delayed, by how much, and what would fix it — which `freshness` deliberately does not. Distinct from freshness: a frame can be perfectly fresh for its lane and still be `delayed` because the caller's plan entitles them to a delayed lane.

mode.description: whether this body is the realtime lane or a delayed one

delay_seconds.description: NEVER FABRICATED. `0` is a positive assertion of live; a delay of unknown magnitude is `null`, never `0` — the two are not interchangeable and a consumer must not treat a null as zero.

reason.description: `plan_tier` = delayed by the caller's entitlement, fixable by upgrading. `source_delay` = the upstream feed itself is delayed, which NO plan changes. null when mode is live. When both apply, `plan_tier` wins — it is the binding, actionable one.

upgrade_tier.description: The internal plan SLUG that would clear the delay (`edge`, `pro`, `ultra`…), or null when nothing would. ⚠️ A SLUG, never a display name — slug `pro` is shown to customers as "Pro" and slug `edge` as "Edge". Always null when `reason` is `source_delay`.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 problem-details error envelope (application/problem+json) returned by the capability middleware and @gate_api.

SuccessEnvelope.description: Generic success envelope. Most reads carry `ok:true`; widget reads also fold in `freshness` and `delivery`.

PagedEnvelope.description: Cursor-paginated envelope (shared ?limit=&cursor= model): `next_cursor` is null on the last page.

ApiKeyBearer.description: API key / PAT / service-account token as a Bearer token.

ApiKeyQuery.name: api_key
ApiKeyQuery.description: API key passed as a query parameter (alternative to the Bearer header).
